title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: An index that forgets what you deleted
summary: Kotlin Jump 1.42.28 fixes what the index remembered wrongly: ghosts of renamed functions after a restart, a "not in equals/copy" hint on every data class property until the file was edited, a workspace class shadowed by its published JAR, a Cmd+T list full of local variables, files of `:app-widgets` filed under `:app`, and folders deleted or renamed in the explorer that stayed navigable.

highlights.title: No more ghosts after a restart
highlights.description: A file restored from the snapshot no longer keeps the entries of an earlier scan, so a renamed function leaves Cmd+T and a deleted class stops resolving.

highlights.title: Snapshot keeps every flag
highlights.description: expect, actual and primary constructor parameters survive a restart: no false "not in equals/copy" hint on data classes, KMP badges back at once.

highlights.title: The right file, the right module
highlights.description: A workspace class beats its JAR copy, Cmd+T skips local variables, a file joins its most specific Gradle module, and a deleted or renamed folder leaves the index.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: Restoring a file from the snapshot replaces its entries instead of stacking them on the ones from an open editor's scan.
Snapshot version 24 persists `expect`, `actual` and primary constructor parameters; `actual` wins over `expect` in any restore order.
Cmd+Click prefers a workspace file over the same symbol in a JAR, and the bundled stdlib over another JAR.
Cmd+T ignores local variables; `:app-widgets` files no longer belong to `:app`, and Windows paths match their module.

Folders deleted or renamed in the explorer or a terminal, and workspace folders added or removed, update the index; a file that outgrew the size limit is emptied; `app/build/**` also excludes in the watchers.
